To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the histological diagnosis of PHHI can be made by a blinded observer, (ii) adenomatosis is not the only histological finding in PHHI, and (iii) diffuse nesidiodyslplasia, which is the predominant histological finding in our study, may be associated with ductuloinsular complex formation and centroacinar hyperplasia.
we have shown that PHH subjects have a spectrum from no abnormality, to subtle changes to florids adenomatosis.
the majority of patients had diffuse changes, and only a small proportion had focal adenomatous lesions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no histological classification of persistent hyperinsulinemic hyperglycemia of infancy.
PHHI is not a single disease entity.
there are no histological criteria to differentiate between focal or diffuse forms of PHHI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a spectrum of histologic changes in PHHI.
PHHI is a heterogeneous condition with diffuse changes in most patients.
the diagnosis of adenomatous hyperplasia is difficult to confirm in the majority of PHHI subjects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diagnosis of PHHI is based on clinical and biochemical features and that histopathology is not a prerequisite for diagnosis.
the diagnosis of adenomatous hyperplasia is not a reliable indicator for focal resection in PHHI patients.
the histologic findings of PHHI are not as clear-cut as originally described and that a single biopsy may not be representative of the entire pancreas.
